topic: Lynch syndrome testing in colorectal cancer

audits.title: 1542 An Audit of Rates of Lynch Testing in Confirmed Colorectal Cancer Cases
audits.standard: NICE 2017: all patients with colorectal cancer tested for Lynch syndrome

cycle1.result: 79% tested for Lynch; biopsy to result 2 to 276 days (average 45); 54% within 30 days, 34% 30–90 days, 12% over 90 days.

audits.other_findings: Results within 30 days rose by year: 30% (2017), 55% (2018), 71% (2019); median days 39, 28 and 16.
audits.citation: Cribb E, Liccardo F, Crisford S, Pawa N. 1542 An Audit of Rates of Lynch Testing in Confirmed Colorectal Cancer Cases. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.173.

audits.title: 313 An Audit of Lynch Syndrome Testing Practices at Kettering General Hospital Against NICE Guidelines
audits.standard: NICE DG27: Lynch syndrome testing for all newly diagnosed colorectal cancer; IHC results within 7–10 days

cycle1.result: All patients had IHC testing; only 15% had IHC results within 7–10 days; only 50% with MMR-deficient results referred for genetic testing.

audits.other_findings: Recommendations include a clinical lead for the testing pathway, inter-specialty collaboration and education.
audits.citation: Abdellatif M, Ahmed M, Hadjidemetriou M, Ramzy A. 313 An Audit of Lynch Syndrome Testing Practices at Kettering General Hospital Against NICE Guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.234.

audits.title: 937 Adherence to MMR Reporting Standards in Newly Diagnosed Colorectal Cancer as Part of the Lynch Syndrome Workup Pathway: A Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: NICE guidance: MMR IHC or MSI testing for all colorectal cancers

cycle1.result: 97% had MMR testing; 90% reported within 10 days; biopsy to histology 8.6 days; MMR to MLH1 result 251 days.

cycle2.result: 100% had MMR testing; 97% reported within 10 days (average 4.3 days); biopsy to histology 8 days; MMR to MLH1 result 91 days.

audits.other_findings: Four patients were MMR deficient, three of whom had BRAF and MLH1 methylation testing.
audits.citation: Sonoo P, Oo Z, Boereboom C. 937 Adherence to MMR Reporting Standards in Newly Diagnosed Colorectal Cancer as Part of the Lynch Syndrome Workup Pathway: A Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.292.

audits.title: TTP2.04 Unravelling the Genetic Enigma of Lynch Syndrome: An Audit of Practice in a District General Hospital
audits.standard: NICE guidelines on Lynch syndrome testing and genetic referral for MMR-deficient colorectal cancer
audits.setting: District general hospital (Airedale General Hospital, West Yorkshire)

cycle1.result: 17 (8.8%) had deficient MMR; genetic testing referrals made for 5 dMMR cases, with 1 missed referral

audits.other_findings: 14 dMMR cases had MLH1 mutations and 3 non-MLH1; the missed referral was promptly followed up.
audits.citation: Hande N. TTP2.04 Unravelling the Genetic Enigma of Lynch Syndrome: An Audit of Practice in a District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_13). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf166.239.

audits.title: From diagnosis of colorectal cancer to diagnosis of Lynch syndrome: The RM Partners quality improvement project.
audits.standard: NICE DG27: universal testing for Lynch syndrome in all newly diagnosed colorectal cancer
audits.setting: Nine colorectal cancer MDTs, RM Partners West London cancer alliance

cycle1.result: Baseline LS pathway audit of 30 consecutive CRC patients per MDT; effective referral for genetic testing 10%.

audits.intervention: LS champion in each MDT, regional project manager and nurse practitioner, online training packages, patient workshops, and 'in-house' mainstreamed genetic testing in oncology clinics.

cycle2.result: Effective referral for genetic testing rose to 74% (p = 0.02); significant improvement in MMR testing on endoscopic biopsies (p = 0.008) and methylation/BRAF testing (p = 0/03 as given).

audits.other_findings: Contributed to a National Lynch Syndrome Transformation Project in England.
audits.citation: Monje-Garcia L, Bill T, Farthing L, Hill N, Kipps E, Brady AF, et al.. From diagnosis of colorectal cancer to diagnosis of Lynch syndrome: The RM Partners quality improvement project. Colorectal Dis. 2023;25(9):1844-1851. doi:10.1111/codi.16707. PMID: 37553835.
